Case Name: Load shell and show login card without a session
Precondition:
1. openan-portal is deployed behind its own nginx entry (container port 8080) and reaches the deployed orchestration-center through BACKEND_URL
2. orchestration-center access authentication is active (its user store holds the built-in admin account, or access_password is set in file mode)
3. The browser context holds no session_token cookie and no localStorage entry for the portal origin
4. The Playwright context sets i18nextLng=en in localStorage before the first navigation
Steps:
1. Open http://<PORTAL_HOST>:8080/ and wait until the login card is visible see result 1
2. Capture the response of GET /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/check issued during boot see result 2
3. Assert the login card controls and the absence of the shell navigation see result 3
4. Cleanup: clear cookies and localStorage for the origin, reload the page and re-check the session see result 4
Expected Result:
1. The document returns 200 with content-type text/html, the title is "OpenAN Portal" and the #root element is populated
2. HTTP 200 with data.auth_required=true and data.authenticated=false
3. The username input (autocomplete=username), the password input and the submit button labelled "Enter" are visible; no header navigation element is rendered and no plugin route container is mounted in the main area (the auth gate returns before routing, so no plugin page can be on screen)
4. After the reload the login card is shown again and GET /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/check returns data.authenticated=false, so the case left no session behind

Case Name: Sign in and render nav from plugin manifests
Precondition:
1. openan-portal and orchestration-center are deployed and the orchestration-center /auth endpoints answer 200
2. The built-in admin account credentials are provided by environment variables, not hardcoded
3. All enabled entries of portal/bundled-plugins.json have their artifacts installed under the portal public /plugins/<id>/
4. The source plugins skill-center and execution-center are enabled in plugins/plugin-overrides.json
Steps:
1. Submit the admin username and password on the login card see result 1
2. Wait for the header navigation container to render see result 2
3. Record every /plugins/<id>/plugin.manifest.json response issued during shell boot see result 3
4. Cleanup: click Logout and verify the server-side session is gone see result 4
Expected Result:
1. POST /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/login returns 200 with data.username=admin and data.role=admin, and sets an HttpOnly session_token cookie
2. The header navigation is rendered with the manifest-driven buttons (the Registry Center and Orchestration Center buttons and the AN Ontology group button are visible) and the login card is no longer in the DOM; nav ordering is asserted only by FIT-openan-portal-plugin-registry-002
3. Six 200 responses, one per enabled id in bundled-plugins.json, each body id equal to the requested id and each body version non-empty
4. POST /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/logout returns 200 and a following GET .../auth/check returns data.authenticated=false

Case Name: Guard deep link until sign-in and resume the route
Precondition:
1. openan-portal and orchestration-center are deployed and orchestration-center serves GET /rest/v1/orchestrate/workflows
2. The browser context has no session_token cookie
3. The orchestration-center bundle declares the /orchestration route and is installed under /plugins/orchestration-center
Steps:
1. Request http://<PORTAL_HOST>:8080/orchestration directly without a session see result 1
2. Sign in as admin and wait for the route content see result 2
3. Cleanup: log out and request /orchestration again see result 3
Expected Result:
1. The document returns 200, the login card is visible, location.pathname stays /orchestration and no orchestration sub-app element is mounted
2. location.pathname is still /orchestration after login, GET /rest/v1/orchestrate/workflows returns 200 and the orchestration sub-app root is rendered
3. The login card is shown again and no GET /rest/v1/orchestrate/workflows request is issued

Case Name: Log out and confirm the session is revoked
Precondition:
1. openan-portal and orchestration-center are deployed and the admin account can sign in
2. The browser context is clean before the case starts
Steps:
1. Sign in as admin and confirm the navigation is rendered see result 1
2. Click the Logout button in the header see result 2
3. Request /registry directly after the logout see result 3
4. Cleanup: reload the page and re-check the session state see result 4
Expected Result:
1. The session_token cookie is present and GET .../auth/check returns data.authenticated=true
2. POST /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/logout returns 200, the session_token cookie is cleared and the login card replaces the shell
3. The login card is visible, location.pathname stays /registry and no /api/registry-center request is issued
4. GET .../auth/check returns data.authenticated=false and only the login card is rendered, i.e. the logout is durable across reloads

Case Name: Toggle theme and keep it after reload
Precondition:
1. openan-portal and orchestration-center are deployed and the admin account can sign in
2. The Playwright context starts with no theme entry in localStorage so the default dark theme applies
Steps:
1. Sign in and assert the default theme state see result 1
2. Click the theme toggle button in the header see result 2
3. Reload the page see result 3
4. Cleanup: click the theme toggle again and re-check the stored preference see result 4
Expected Result:
1. The html element carries the class dark, document.documentElement.style.colorScheme equals "dark" and localStorage theme equals "dark"
2. The dark class is removed from the html element, colorScheme equals "light" and localStorage theme equals "light"
3. After the reload the html element still has no dark class and localStorage theme equals "light"
4. The dark class is back on the html element and localStorage theme equals "dark", restoring the default for the next case

Case Name: Share one session across mounted sub-apps
Precondition:
1. openan-portal, registry-center and orchestration-center are deployed and reachable through the portal nginx proxies
2. Both sub-app bundles are installed and enabled in bundled-plugins.json
3. The admin account can sign in to the portal and the registry holds at least one AgentCard
Steps:
1. Sign in once at the portal entry see result 1
2. Navigate to /registry, then /orchestration, then back to /registry see result 2
3. Inspect the session credential attached to each sub-app request see result 3
4. Cleanup: log out and re-open /registry see result 4
Expected Result:
1. The session_token cookie is HttpOnly and GET .../auth/check returns data.authenticated=true
2. Every sub-app API request during the three navigations returns 200 and the login card never appears
3. The /api/registry-center/rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards/manage request and the /rest/v1/orchestrate/workflows request both carried the same session_token cookie value, proving one session is shared across sub-apps
4. GET .../auth/check returns data.authenticated=false and /registry renders the login card with no /api/registry-center request issued

3. A reusable signed-in storage state (session_token cookie) is captured inside the case before the bookmark navigations
Steps:
1. Sign in, then open a fresh page at http://<PORTAL_HOST>:8080/orchestration see result 1
2. Assert that the shell boots directly into the sub-app see result 2
3. Repeat the fresh navigation for /registry see result 3
4. Cleanup: log out, then re-open the bookmarked URL see result 4
Expected Result:

Case Name: Keep host session when sub-app API returns 401
Precondition:
1. openan-portal, registry-center and orchestration-center are deployed and the admin account can sign in
2. The registry-center manifest declares backend.gateway /api/registry-center without authScope, so the component scope applies
3. The Playwright context can intercept requests to /api/registry-center/**
Steps:
1. Sign in, open /registry, then intercept /api/registry-center/** to answer 401 and reload the route see result 1
2. Assert the host authentication state after the component failure see result 2
3. Cleanup: remove the interception, reload and re-assert the sub-app data path see result 3
Expected Result:
1. The URL stays /registry, the login card is not rendered and the header still exposes the Logout button
2. GET /api/orchestrate/rest/v1/orchestrate/auth/check still returns data.authenticated=true and no auth-expired redirect happened, so a component-scope 401 does not clear the host session
3. GET /api/registry-center/rest/v1/registry-center/agent-cards/manage returns 200 again and the agent list is rendered

Case Name: Keep plugin preference when server sync is missing
Precondition:
1. openan-portal and orchestration-center are deployed and the admin account can sign in
2. Execution Center is enabled as a source plugin and its /execution route resolves inside the portal
3. The deployed orchestration-center exposes no /auth/plugins endpoint, so per-user preference sync is unavailable and the browser-local list is authoritative
Steps:
1. Sign in and open Plugin Management from the Settings menu see result 1
2. Toggle the Execution Center plugin off see result 2
3. Reload the page see result 3
4. Cleanup: toggle Execution Center back on and re-assert the stored preference see result 4
Expected Result:
1. The Plugin Management dialog is rendered and no role=alert banner or login card appears; the absent /auth/plugins route does not block the shell, which keeps browser-local preferences
2. The nav no longer renders Execution Center and localStorage openan-disabled-plugins equals ["execution-center"], i.e. the change is applied locally without any server-side preference store
3. After the reload the disabled state is still applied (Execution Center absent from the nav) because it is read from localStorage
4. The nav renders Execution Center again and localStorage openan-disabled-plugins equals [], so the case left no preference behind; the missing /auth/plugins endpoint stays recorded as the plan risk
